core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Hadad corresponds to the Arabic form حداد (Arabic root ح د د (ḥ-d-d); حدّاد (Ḥaddād)). Its core sense is iron; smith, ironworker. Hadad is Arabic حدّاد (Ḥaddād) 'blacksmith, ironworker' (from حديد 'iron'). The source gloss 'thunder' belongs to the Semitic storm-god Hadad (a different, ancient Near-Eastern name) — a plausible confusion, but not the Arabic word; the 'smith' sense is recorded for this form. Same name as haddad.
